turns.prompt_text: I take a lot of photos and I have a lot of trouble organizing them
turns.response_html:
Managing a massive photo library is a common headache, but a few strategic moves can turn that digital clutter into a searchable archive.

Organize Your Digital Gallery

  • Consolidate First: Move all images from SD cards, hard drives, and old phones into one primary cloud service (like Google Photos or iCloud).
  • Leverage AI Search: Stop manual sorting; use keywords like "sunset," "receipt," or "dog" to let the software's recognition engine find what you need instantly.
  • The "One-Touch" Rule: Every Sunday, spend five minutes deleting blurry shots, screenshots, and duplicates from the past week.
  • Folder Hierarchy: If you prefer manual folders, organize them by Year > Month > Event Name to keep the structure predictable.
  • Favorite the Best: Use the "Heart" or "Star" icon on your top 5% of photos. This creates an automatic "Best Of" album for quick sharing.

Would you like me to look through your Google Photos to help identify specific albums or themes you should group together?
